entry_rationale: AU is eligible and the frozen AONIA strip is the underpriced hawk. Short/pay so the expected mark is higher.
entry_thesis: Keep paying Sep-27 SOFR: official SOFR is still 3.88 while the contract sits at 4.905, and a US 10-year at 5.29 with Brent above 100 is not an early-easing tape. Mar-27 CORRA at 3.09 versus cash 2.30 still looks light if Canada has to import that same persistence, so the existing pay stays. The clearer underpriced hawk risk is Australia—Jun-27 AONIA at 4.91 is only 31 bp above cash 4.60 despite an AU 10-year at 5.245—so pay AONIA Jun-27 rather than chase already-extended USD crosses.

events.rationale: AU is eligible and the frozen AONIA strip is the underpriced hawk. Short/pay so the expected mark is higher.

invalidation: The view breaks if the US 10-year reverses away from the 2002 high together with a break in oil while Sep-27 SOFR and Jun-27 AONIA stop repricing higher, or if Jun-27 AONIA trades up through the AU 10-year at 5.245 and the cash-to-contract gap is closed.
